admission.workflow: Render the complete pinned Codicon glyph library through a static Proctor semantic-icon catalog with exact font assets, accessible labeling, supported sizes, disabled state, reduced-motion-aware progress animation, and no raw glyph-name contract for product callers.

items.rationale: The Microsoft MIT text covering the admitted TypeScript source is preserved locally.

Preserve the complete built-in and derived Codicon catalog composition. Type-only import annotations make declaration dependencies explicit under Proctor's executable-cycle checks; the implementation is otherwise preserved.
Preserve every registered Codicon glyph identifier and exact font character from the pinned source.

Preserve registration, aliases, validation, and font-character lookup for the complete library. Type-only import annotations make declaration dependencies explicit under Proctor's executable-cycle checks; the implementation is otherwise preserved.
Preserve ThemeIcon parsing, modifier, equality, and classification behavior required by admitted icon consumers.
Retain exact font loading, smoothing, sizing, and intrinsic inline behavior behind a single Proctor-owned root and semantic DOM contract.
The disabled opacity and throttled centered spin behavior inform the semantic modifier implementation; reduced-motion suppression is added by Proctor policy.
Confirms that the font asset is supplied by the external @vscode/codicons package rather than the VS Code source tree.

dependencies.rationale: Supplies the exact unmodified CC-BY-4.0 font used by the pinned VS Code source; dependency admission, hash verification, and attribution are tracked separately.
The admitted base runtime supplies string classification and disposal contracts.

divergences.summary: Product callers select static Proctor semantic icon identifiers; raw Codicon names, CSS classes, and arbitrary theme icon registration remain internal implementation details.
The browser adapter owns one prctr root, supports only standard sizes and explicit modifiers, hides decorative icons, labels meaningful icons, and suppresses continuous spin for reduced motion.
Type-only import annotations preserve upstream compiler elision while making the runtime dependency graph explicit. These source edits are adaptations rather than undeclared copy transformations.

verification.obligation: Verify the static catalog is ordered, unique, complete enough for admitted product roles, and every identifier resolves to a valid font character without exposing glyph names.
Verify the exact package version, declared license, and SHA-256 of the bundled font.
Verify the production browser adapter, font bundle, semantic identifiers, standard sizing, modifiers, and decorative versus meaningful accessibility semantics in sandboxed Chromium.
Verify one TypeScript stylesheet owner, accepted cascade layers, a single Proctor root, namespaced custom properties, and no id selectors or unreviewed important declarations.
Verify schema, local digest, marker, license reference, unique ownership, divergence, and evidence parity without a VS Code checkout.
Resolve the exact VS Code commit and verify every reviewed upstream blob against the canonical checkout.
